summary: The root جَذَّ (jadhdha) primarily means to cut off or sever something completely and quickly. It implies a decisive and final separation, often leaving no trace or connection behind.

provenance.lane: Edward William Lane, An Arabic-English Lexicon (1863-93), public domain. Digital text via Perseus, Tufts University, CC BY-SA 3.0 US.

headwords.def: جَ َّهُ, (S, A, L, Msb,) aor. جَ ُ َ, (L, Msb,) inf. n. جَ ٌّ, (L, Msb, K,) He cut it, or cut it off; (S, A, L, Msb;) namely, a thing; (S, Msb;) as, for instance, a rope: (L:) or he cut it off utterly; (L, K;) and جَ ْجَ َةٌ [inf. n. of ] signifies the same as جَ ٌّ, i. e. the cutting off utterly: (K:) and اِجْتِ َا ٌ [inf. n.

انج ّ It became cut, or cut off: (S, L, Msb, K:) or cut off utterly: or cut off utterly and quickly: and in like manner, [said of a number of things, or used in a frequentative or an intensive sense; being quasi-pass. of 2]. (L.)
R. Q. 1 جَ ْجَ َ, inf. n. جَ ْجَ َةٌ: see 1.

جَ ٌّ A piece broken off; a fragment: pl. أَجْ َا ٌ: so in the phrase, كَسَرْتُهُ أَجْ َا ًا [ I broke it in pieces, or fragments ]; occurring in a trad., relating to an idol. (L.) [See also جُ َا ٌ.]
مَا عَلَيْهِ جُ َّةٌ There is not upon him a piece of rag; i. e., any garment to cover him: (L:) or anything (S, L, K) of clothing: (S, L:) pl. جُ َ ٌ. (Bd in xxi. 59.)

جَ َا ٌ, with fet-h, The act of separating a thing from another thing ( فَصْلُ شَىْءٍ عَنْ شَىْءٍ, accord. to some copies of the K and the TA; [see 1;] accord. to other copies of the K, [probably by mistranscription,] the superiority of a thing over another thing, فَضْلُ شىءٍ عَلَى شىءٍ ); as also. (K.) See also what next follows.

جُ َا ٌ and, (S, L, K,) the former of which is the more chaste, (S, L,) and, (L, K,) substs. from جَ ٌّ the act of “ breaking; “ (K;) What is broken, of, or from, a thing: (S, L:) or what is broken, or cut, in pieces: or broken pieces: so in the Kur xxi. 59, in which the word is read in these three different forms: (L:) some also read جُ ُ ًا, which is pl. of; and some, جُ َ ًا, pl. of جُ َّةٌ: (Bd:) or the first signifies fragments of a thing much broken; [as a coll. gen. n.;] and the n. un.
جِ َا ٌ: see جُ َا ٌ, in four places.

جَ ِي ٌ and Cut; or cut off: or cut off utterly: or cut off utterly and quickly: and also broken: (L:) pl. of the former, جُ ُ ٌ and جِ َا ٌ (Bd in xxi. 59) and جُ َا ٌ, which last is extr. (L. See the paragraph headed جُ َا ٌ, in three places.) Also the former, (A, K,) and شَرَابٌ جَ ِي ٌ, (A,) and, (S, L, K,) Meal of parched barley or wheat; syn. سَوِيقٌ; (S, A, L, K;) so prepared [ by being moistened with water or with clarified butter &c.
جُ َا َةٌ and its pl. جُ َا َتٌ: see جُ َا ٌ, in two places.
جَ ِي َةٌ: see جَ ِي ٌ, in two places.

يَدْ جَ َّآءُ [fem. of أَجَ ُّ ] (tropical:) An amputated arm or hand: used figuratively: see أَحَ ُّ, in art. ح. (L.) رَحِمٌ جَ َّآءُ (assumed tropical:) A bond of relationship [ cut, or severed, or] not made close by affection; expl. by إِ َا لَمْ تُوصَلْ [a well-known phrase: erroneously explained by Golius as meaning “ uterus infœcundus vel interruptæ conceptionis ” ]: (Fr, S, L, K:) as also حَ َّآءُ. (Fr, S, L.) يَمِينٌ جَ َّآءُ: see حَ َّآءُ.

جَ َّانٌ (As, L, and so in some copies of the K: in other copies of the K, and in the TA, جُ َّانٌ:) Soft stones: (As, L, K:) as also كَ َّانٌ [q. v.]: (As, L:) n. un. (of both, As, L) with ة. (As, L, K.)
مَجْ ُو ٌ: see جَ ِي ٌ. عَطَآءٌ غَيْرُ مَجْ ُو ٍ [ A gift, or stipend, ] not cut short, or not interrupted; syn. غَيْرُ مَقْطُوعٍ. (A'Obeyd, S, L.)

headword_note: Lane indexes geminate roots with two letters where the Corpus uses three; both spellings are resolved here.
